newsitem.title: FRANCE: France raises 96 grain crop estimate to 61.55 mln.
newsitem.headline: France raises 96 grain crop estimate to 61.55 mln.

text.p: The French farm ministry said on Friday it raised its estimate for the 1996 grain crop to 61.55 million tonnes from a previous target of 61.01 million tonnes. This would compare with a 1995 crop of 53.55 million tonnes.

In its latest estimate as of October 1, the ministry also raised its forecast for the 1996 soft wheat crop to 34.57 million tonnes from last month's target of 34.15 million and from 29.85 million produced in 1995.
The new estimate for the national grain crop assumes an average grain yield of 6.98 tonnes per hectare against 6.92 tonnes last month and 6.46 tonnes last year.
Total grain sowings were put at 8.818 million hectares against 8.819 million last month and 8.298 million last year.
The ministry raised its estimate for the national soft wheat yield to 7.25 tonnes per hectare from 7.16 tonnes last month and 6.61 tonnes last year.
The new wheat estimate assumes sowings of 4.768 million hectares against 4.766 million last month and 4.516 million last year.
France also raised its estimate for the 1996 barley crop to 9.38 million tonnes from the 9.31 million forecast last month and the 7.69 million produced last year.
The new barley crop estimate is based on projected yields of 6.13 tonnes per hectare against 6.09 tonnes last month and 5.54 tonnes last year.
Barley area was put at 1.530 million hectares against 1.528 million last month and 1.387 million last year.
The ministry slightly cut its estimate for the French maize crop to 13.78 million tonnes from a previous target of 13.81 million. This would compare with a 1995 crop of 12.74 million tonnes.
It put at 8.01 tonnes per hectare its estimate for the 1996 maize yield against 7.99 tonnes last month and 7.69 tonnes last year.
But it slightly cut its estimate for 1996 maize sowings to 1.722 million hectares from 1.728 million last month. This would compare with sowings of 1.656 million hectares in 1995.
